findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — A single provider rejection aborts the whole cancellation loop before its lazy Prisma deletions execute, so retries replay successfully cancelled batches that [SendGrid rejects with HTTP 400](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/cancel-scheduled-sends/cancel-or-pause-a-scheduled-send) and strand subsequent reminders until delivery.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Deferring every scheduled cancellation to cron can cross [SendGrid's ten-minute cancellation deadline](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/cancel-scheduled-sends), allowing a reminder cancelled just before that deadline to be delivered despite the booking cancellation succeeding.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Reminder persistence moved from awaited Prisma operations into unawaited helpers that swallow database errors, allowing cancellation to report success while unscheduled reminders remain eligible for later delivery and scheduled emails never receive their cancellation marker.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — The new cancellation request uses an unauthenticated client because sgMail.setApiKey configures a [separate client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-nodejs/main/packages/mail/src/classes/mail-service.js), so deferred cancellations fail with HTTP 401.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — One rejected cancellation aborts the entire loop and skips queued database deletions, preventing cancellation of all subsequent reminders.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Paginate cancellation work with bounded concurrency, since this unbounded query feeds serial SendGrid calls that can exhaust the cron request duration after bulk workflow changes and prevent pending emails from being scheduled.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid cancellation failure aborts the entire batch before queued Prisma deletions execute, leaving subsequent cancelled reminders scheduled and retrying already successful cancellations.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — The replacement cancellation calls are unawaited, so request completion can interrupt cancellation flags and unscheduled-reminder deletions that previously completed before responding.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Add a batch cancellation test with a middle SendGrid rejection to verify earlier successful cancellations are persisted and later reminders still get processed.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Add a cancellation test with delayed reminder database operations to verify the handler waits for cancelled flags and unscheduled reminder deletions before returning success.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — A single provider rejection aborts the whole cancellation loop before its lazy Prisma deletions execute, so retries replay successfully cancelled batches that [SendGrid rejects with HTTP 400](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/cancel-scheduled-sends/cancel-or-pause-a-scheduled-send) and strand subsequent reminders until delivery.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 54-80 that the cancellation loop iterates through remindersToCancel, making SendGrid API calls and collecting Prisma delete operations. If any SendGrid request fails (throws), the catch block at line 79 only logs the error and the loop terminates early. The workflowRemindersToDelete array contains lazy Prisma operations that are only executed by Promise.all at line 77, which won't be reached if an error occurs mid-loop. This means: 1) Successfully cancelled SendGrid batches before the failure won't have their DB records deleted, 2) Subsequent reminders in the array won't be processed at all. On retry, the already-cancelled SendGrid batches may return errors (400) since they're already cancelled, causing the same failure pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Deferring every scheduled cancellation to cron can cross [SendGrid's ten-minute cancellation deadline](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/cancel-scheduled-sends), allowing a reminder cancelled just before that deadline to be delivered despite the booking cancellation succeeding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that deleteScheduledEmailReminder now sets 'cancelled: true' in the database instead of immediately canceling with SendGrid (unless immediateDelete is true). The cron job in scheduleEmailReminders.ts processes reminders with 'cancelled: true' that are scheduled within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled less than 10 minutes before the scheduled send time, the cron may not run in time to cancel the SendGrid batch before SendGrid's cancellation deadline passes, resulting in the email being sent despite the booking being cancelled. This is a real timing bug where the deferred cancellation approach can fail to meet SendGrid's constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — One rejected cancellation aborts the entire loop and skips queued database deletions, preventing cancellation of all subsequent reminders.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 52-75, the code iterates through remindersToCancel with a for...of loop, making await calls to client.request() for each reminder. If any single client.request() call throws an error, the catch block at line 73 catches it and logs the error, but by that point the loop has already been aborted. This means subsequent reminders won't be cancelled, and the workflowRemindersToDelete array won't contain all the delete operations. The Promise.all at line 71 only runs for reminders processed before the error. This is a real bug where one failed API call prevents cancellation of all remaining reminders in the batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Paginate cancellation work with bounded concurrency, since this unbounded query feeds serial SendGrid calls that can exhaust the cron request duration after bulk workflow changes and prevent pending emails from being scheduled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new query at line 44 that fetches all cancelled reminders within the next hour without any limit/pagination, then processes them serially with SendGrid API calls in a for loop. This is a legitimate scalability concern - if many bookings are cancelled/rescheduled, this unbounded query and serial processing could indeed exhaust cron timeout. The finding correctly identifies specific code in the diff (the findMany without limit, the serial for loop with await client.request). This is a real architectural concern introduced by the new code, though not a bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid cancellation failure aborts the entire batch before queued Prisma deletions execute, leaving subsequent cancelled reminders scheduled and retrying already successful cancellations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 52-75, the loop iterates through remindersToCancel, making a SendGrid API call for each reminder, then pushing a Prisma delete to workflowRemindersToDelete array. If any SendGrid request fails (throws), the catch block at line 73 catches it and logs the error, but by that point: 1) Some reminders may have been successfully cancelled in SendGrid but their Prisma deletes haven't executed yet (Promise.all is at line 72), 2) Subsequent reminders in the loop won't be processed at all. This means a single failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state where some reminders are cancelled in SendGrid but not deleted from DB, and others remain scheduled. The finding accurately identifies this batch processing issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — The replacement cancellation calls are unawaited, so request completion can interrupt cancellation flags and unscheduled-reminder deletions that previously completed before responding.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in handleCancelBooking.ts, the old code used `remindersToDelete.push(reminderToDelete)` to collect PrismaPromises and then awaited them via `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. The new code removes this collection and just calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without awaiting them. Looking at the implementations in emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts, these are async functions that perform database operations (prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete). Since they're not awaited, the request could complete before these operations finish, potentially leaving reminders in an inconsistent state. This is a real bug where async operations are fire-and-forget when they should be awaited.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Add a batch cancellation test with a middle SendGrid rejection to verify earlier successful cancellations are persisted and later reminders still get processed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new code in scheduleEmailReminders.ts (lines 42-75) that iterates through reminders, makes SendGrid API calls, and collects delete promises. If a SendGrid request fails mid-loop, the error is caught but earlier successful cancellations may have already been processed while later ones are skipped. The finding correctly identifies that this new batch cancellation logic lacks test coverage for partial failure scenarios. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic, though it's a suggestion for testing rather than a bug in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Add a cancellation test with delayed reminder database operations to verify the handler waits for cancelled flags and unscheduled reminder deletions before returning success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows significant changes to how workflow reminders are cancelled - instead of immediately deleting reminders, the code now sets a 'cancelled' flag and relies on a separate cron job (scheduleEmailReminders.ts) to process cancellations. In handleCancelBooking.ts, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are made without awaiting them, and the remindersToDelete array was removed. This is a real architectural change that introduces eventual consistency. The finding correctly identifies that testing this new async cancellation flow would be valuable to ensure the handler properly handles the delayed database operations. However, this is a test suggestion for new functionality rather than a bug.
